question: What is the primary histological nature of cervical polyps?
explanation: Cervical polyps are primarily benign, non-cancerous hyperplastic growths originating from the cervical tissue. [learn more](GNS216_U5_T15#GNS216_U5_T15_h1)

question: How do most cervical polyps typically attach to the cervical tissue?

options.A: By deep invasion into the myometrium
options.C: Via a network of fragile fibrous roots
options.D: Via a thin stalk called a peduncle

explanation: Most cervical polyps are pedunculated, meaning they hang from the cervical surface by a slender stalk or peduncle. [learn more](GNS216_U5_T15#GNS216_U5_T15_h1)

question: Which hormone is primarily implicated in stimulating the proliferation of cervical polyp tissue?
explanation: Elevated or fluctuating levels of estrogen drive the cellular proliferation seen in the development of cervical polyps. [learn more](GNS216_U5_T15#GNS216_U5_T15_h2)

question: A 45-year-old multiparous woman presents with chronic cervicitis and fluctuating hormonal levels. What is her primary predisposing condition for developing cervical polyps?

options.A: Complete obliteration of the internal cervical os by fibrous scar tissue
options.B: Rapid malignant degeneration of squamous epithelial basement membranes
options.C: Severe systemic autoimmune destruction of the lower uterine segment
options.D: Localized tissue proliferation driven by chronic inflammation and estrogen

explanation: Chronic inflammation combined with estrogen stimulation creates an ideal environment for localized tissue overgrowth and polyp formation. [learn more](GNS216_U5_T15#GNS216_U5_T15_h2)

question: What is the most common presenting symptom of a symptomatic cervical polyp?
explanation: Due to their fragile blood vessels, polyps commonly bleed, presenting as intermenstrual, postcoital, or postmenopausal bleeding. [learn more](GNS216_U5_T15#GNS216_U5_T15_h3)

question: Why do cervical polyps frequently cause bleeding following sexual intercourse?

options.A: Friction completely dissolves the cervical mucosal lining within seconds
options.B: Intercourse causes immediate necrosis and shedding of the entire myometrium
options.C: The surface of the polyp contains fragile, congested blood vessels prone to trauma
options.D: The muscular wall of the cervix forcefully ruptures during coitus

explanation: Physical friction during coitus easily traumatizes the delicate, hyperemic blood vessels on the surface of the protruding polyp. [learn more](GNS216_U5_T15#GNS216_U5_T15_h3)

question: What is the definitive diagnostic and management step required after visualizing a suspected cervical polyp?

options.A: Serial observation without any physical intervention
options.B: Immediate commencement of high-dose systemic chemotherapy
options.C: Histopathological examination of the removed tissue
options.D: Application of topical caustic antiseptic solutions only

explanation: Every removed polyp must undergo histological analysis to definitively rule out cellular atypia or malignancy. [learn more](GNS216_U5_T15#GNS216_U5_T15_h4)

question: Which nursing action is most appropriate when preparing a patient for a speculum examination to assess for cervical polyps?

options.A: Instruct the patient to maintain a standing position throughout the inspection
options.B: Insert an indwelling urinary catheter to completely empty the bladder
options.C: Administer general anesthesia before allowing the clinician into the examination room
options.D: Explain the procedure, ensure privacy, and place the patient in the lithotomy position

explanation: Proper positioning, clear communication, and maintaining privacy reduce patient anxiety and facilitate adequate visualization of the cervix. [learn more](GNS216_U5_T15#GNS216_U5_T15_h4)

question: What is the primary intervention for managing a symptomatic cervical polyp?

options.B: Radiation therapy directed at the lower uterine segment
options.C: Surgical removal via simple avulsion or snip polypectomy
options.D: Long-term oral antibiotic therapy to shrink tissue mass

explanation: Polypectomy is a straightforward procedure that relieves symptoms and provides tissue for mandatory biopsy. [learn more](GNS216_U5_T15#GNS216_U5_T15_h5)

question: Why is medical drug therapy rarely used as a primary standalone cure for cervical polyps?

options.A: Pharmacological agents cause immediate rupture of the uterine wall
options.B: Hormonal pills stimulate rapid growth rather than regression
options.C: Drugs are completely metabolized before reaching the pelvic cavity
options.D: Medications cannot eliminate established fibrous or hyperplastic tissue structures

explanation: Once a physical polyp mass has formed, pharmacological agents cannot dissolve the structural tissue, necessitating mechanical removal. [learn more](GNS216_U5_T15#GNS216_U5_T15_h5)

question: Which activity should the nurse instruct the patient to avoid immediately following a cervical polypectomy?

options.A: Consuming a normal, balanced nutritional diet
options.B: Using vaginal tampons and engaging in sexual intercourse
options.C: Walking short distances around the hospital ward
options.D: Drinking adequate volumes of plain oral water

explanation: Avoiding tampons and intercourse reduces the risk of introducing bacteria into the healing cervical site and prevents hemorrhage. [learn more](GNS216_U5_T15#GNS216_U5_T15_h6)

question: A patient calls the clinic reporting bright red vaginal bleeding soaking two pads an hour three days after undergoing a cervical polypectomy. What is the most appropriate nursing response?

options.A: Recommend immediate insertion of a medicated vaginal suppository
options.B: Reassure the patient that soaking two pads an hour is a normal finding
options.C: Instruct the patient to double her oral fluid intake and rest in bed
options.D: Advise the patient to report to the clinic immediately for medical evaluation

explanation: Heavy bleeding exceeding normal post-procedure spotting indicates potential hemorrhage and requires prompt clinical assessment. [learn more](GNS216_U5_T15#GNS216_U5_T15_h6)
